transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi Dr. Smith. I guess I'm here because... I just don't care about anything anymore. It's like, everything I used to like doing is just gone. I used to take these art classes, you know? Watercolors mostly. My instructor was this really sweet lady, Mrs. Higgins, she always wore these huge, chunky turquoise necklaces. I think she got them in New Mexico or something. I went there once when I was a kid, the sky is so big there. But yeah, I don't care about the art anymore. Or board-game nights, or hiking, or... I was even thinking about getting back on my old soccer team, but now... I just sit in my room. I just sit there and watch everything slip away. My room gets so dusty, too. I don't know where all the dust comes from. It's just everywhere.
How long have you been feeling this way—not caring about the things you used to enjoy?

Um, well, it got really constant around the summer... so it's been about a year and four months now of it just being like this every day. I know it was summer because the air conditioning in my room broke, and it was just sweltering. The repair guy took almost three weeks to come out. He drove this huge, rusty red van that parked right on the grass outside my window, and it smelled exactly like stale french fries. I used to love french fries, especially the curly ones from that little diner on 4th Street. They closed down a while ago, though. I think they turned the building into a dry cleaner. I never really understood how dry cleaning works, honestly. Like, they don't use water, but it still cleans the clothes? It just seems fake, you know? Like a trick. But yeah... it's been about a year and four months of just not caring.

Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or longer, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it was very different from how you're feeling now?

Um, no... I don't think so. Energetic isn't really a word I'd use for myself. I definitely don't feel elated. If anything, I sleep way too much, even though my mattress is terrible. It has this huge dip right in the middle. I bought it at this weird discount warehouse place years ago when I was still taking a few classes at the community college. The guy who sold it to me was missing half of his left eyebrow. I just kept staring at it while he was talking, trying to figure out if it was a scar from a burn or if he just shaved it wrong by accident, you know? Like, how do you only lose exactly half an eyebrow? It looked so strange. But yeah, no, I've never had a time where I didn't need sleep or felt super happy or anything like that. I just feel heavy all the time. Like that mattress, honestly... it weighed an absolute ton when we had to carry it up the stairs.
During this past year and four months, have you had any thoughts of death or of hurting yourself?

Um... yeah. I keep having these thoughts that I just... I don't want to wake up anymore. It just feels like too much. My friend actually came over and found me recently, and I guess I had been saying out loud that I just couldn't keep living like this. She has a spare key to my place because she used to come over to water my plants when I would go visit my aunt. My aunt lives in Florida, right near the beach, but she absolutely hates the sand. Isn't that funny? Moving to Florida and hating sand. She collects these little glass figurines instead, like tiny glass frogs and owls. They get so dusty, just like my room. She has this one owl that has a chipped wing from when her cat knocked it off the windowsill. That cat was huge, an orange tabby named Marmalade. He used to eat cantaloupe. I've never seen a cat eat fruit before, he would just go crazy for it whenever she cut one open. It smelled so sweet. But yeah... she found me saying I couldn't live like this anymore.
During this past year and four months, has there been any stretch of at least two months where you felt back to your normal self, without these symptoms?

No, there hasn't been any break at all. Like I said, it started being this constant, heavy feeling around the summer... so it's been the whole year and four months without letting up. Not even for a day, let alone two months. I don't even know what my normal self would feel like anymore. Probably like how I felt before I bought that awful mattress. I really should just throw it out. You can actually schedule the city to come pick up large items like that on the first Tuesday of the month, but you have to put a special yellow sticker on it. I don't know where you get the stickers, though. Maybe the post office? The post office near me always smells like wet cardboard, and the line is always out the door because they only ever have one person working at the counter. He wears these thick glasses that magnify his eyes so much they look like cartoon eyes. It's really distracting when you're just trying to buy stamps. But yeah, to answer your question, it's just been the same constant depression for the whole year and four months. No breaks.

During this time, have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds others don't hear, or having beliefs that others have told you aren't true or don't make sense—like feeling you're being watched, punished, or that something is deeply wrong with you in a way that isn't based in reality?

Um... yeah. Actually, yes. I do hear... there's this woman's voice. She talks to me from the corner of my room. It's so clear, like she's standing right next to my bed, just telling me that I ruined everything and that I should just stay inside. She's always in that one corner, right next to this floor lamp I have. The lampshade on it is this really ugly mustard yellow color. I tried to clean it once with a damp sponge because it was getting so dusty, but it just left these massive water spots all over the fabric. I think it's silk, or maybe faux silk? You're definitely not supposed to get it wet, I guess. I bought it at a garage sale a few years ago from this lady who had, I kid you not, like twenty different vintage birdcages just sitting all over her front lawn. None of them even had birds in them, they just had fake plastic ivy woven through the metal bars. It was so bizarre. I always wondered what she did with all those cages when it snowed. Like, do you just leave them out to rust? It seems like a waste. But anyway... yeah, the voice sounds as real as you talking to me right now, just standing by my bed telling me I ruined it all.
